A_seams.criterion: blend-band cells where B1 is steeper than R1 + 0.5 and steeper than the core p99 (2.16); failure if any cluster > 0.25 ha
A_seams.cause: Two mechanisms. (1) Too high: the west arm (nw-cape end) and the Vesttind north buttress are still 50-66 m above R1 (locally up to 140 m) where the blend weight falls to 0 at the frozen coast band (coastFreezeM 70 m, coastFeatherM 160 m), so the difference is absorbed in a ~160 m strip and the slope doubles (about 2.5 against R1 1.3-1.6). (2) Too low: at the north-arm headland the carved north cirque and its trough end up to 190 m below R1 just inside the coast feather, so B1 steps up into the frozen R1 cliff. A smaller cluster lies beside the protected windward-gully corridor, where the fjell flank meets the corridor fade.
A_seams.visibleConsequence: Short, over-steep steps where the west arm and the Vesttind north buttress meet the coast: an artificial sea cliff rather than an arm running down to the sea. A raised lip where the north cirque trough meets the frozen R1 cliff at the headland. A steep bank beside the windward gully. All four fail the declared 0.25 ha limit.
A_seams.b2Strategy: Make the coast an authored boundary condition, not a freeze: give every arm a declared terminal profile that reaches R1 coast heights at the coast band (for example an end-cap level ramp tied to the R1 value at distance 70 m), let cirque troughs exit through authored coastal notches or hang above the R1 cliff with a declared lip, and widen protected-corridor fades to the local relief. Re-run the same seam criterion unchanged.

B_westernCol.cause: At the authored col point the highest authored part is not the west arm (666 m, as designed) but the south-east arm (726 m): that arm starts at the summit, and its radial end cap behind the summit (end taper 160 m, then a 0.9 fall) still stands 726 m high 250 m west of S0. The smooth-max union keeps it, so the col point is filled to about 729 m. The real low point of the S0-S1 crest moves 100 m west to the arm-west/plateau junction, where the Vestfjell plateau shoulder holds it at 695 m. Vesttind keeps 40 m of prominence instead of the authored 56 m.

dryHollows.meaning: a closed hollow in the authored surface that the epsilon priority flood turned into a nearly flat, outward-draining floor; geomorphologically a tarn site, rendered dry because B1 has no water-surface variant

C_hydrology.lakeAndRiverLevels: unchanged: the water-surface raster is shared with R1 and no terrain under any water cell changed, so every lake level (High Tarn 360 m) and channel bed/water level is as in R1

classification.acceptable authored change: drainage reassignment inside the study area following the new cirques and troughs (the north-coast and central-trough catchments gain, High Tarn loses about 7 ha of its west slope)
classification.defect: none found for sinks or unresolved flow; one dry tarn-site hollow is a representation gap (no water-surface variant), not a drainage failure

D_route.note: Controller traversal proves only that the 0.7 step rule is never exceeded; cross-slope above 0.5 means the tread is a traverse on a steep slope and would need a built bench to be comfortable.
